template: In Grafana, create a NEW dashboard (Dashboards menu > New dashboard > Add visualization, or the + Create > Dashboard button). First, if the new dashboard opens with a default panel editor, set the visualization type to Stat and set the panel title to exactly: {{v2}}. For the panel's data source / query, select the data source named TestData (it may be called 'TestData DB' or 'grafana-testdata-datasource' — pick the TestData one). Configure the query so it returns data (e.g. the default scenario is fine, such as 'Random Walk' or 'Current Time' — whatever the TestData source defaults to). Apply the panel. Then save the dashboard with the title exactly: {{v3}} (use the save icon / Save dashboard shortcut, enter the title, and confirm Save). Verify the dashboard is saved (no unsaved-changes indicator) and report the dashboard's URL from the browser address bar, the panel title shown, and the data source name used by the panel.

reportTemplate.summary: From the Service Health dashboard I used New > New dashboard (which opened the default panel editor), switched the visualization type to Stat, set the panel title to exactly "{{v2}}", kept the data source as TestData (the Data source picker showed "TestData" and the query editor rendered the TestData Random Walk scenario fields, so the panel uses the TestData DB / grafana-testdata-datasource plugin with its default Random Walk query), and applied the panel, which rendered a live value ("A-series" 68.3). I then saved the dashboard with the title exactly "{{v3}}" via the save dialog (Details tab, Save): the save dialog closed, the page left edit mode, the URL changed to the new dashboard uid/slug, and the breadcrumb and dashboard heading read "{{v3}}" with the panel heading "{{v2}}" rendered in view mode — i.e. the dashboard is saved, not in edit state. Verified from the live DOM: final URL, dashboard title, panel title, panel rendering and the TestData data source.

values.datasource_name: TestData (TestData DB / grafana-testdata-datasource); picker placeholder "TestData", query editor showed Random Walk scenario fields
